return await tools.progress.append_progress({content: "FINAL ANSWER (complete proposal, one block).

METRIC: HYPERBOLIC_CELL_SILHOUETTE
TITLE: Size-weighted geodesic silhouette of the level-1 SID partition in the frozen reference geometry
FORMULA: Fix curvature c = 1. Let B = {x in R^d : ||x||_2 < 1} be the Poincare ball of curvature -c, with d the reference target-vector dimension. Restrict every sum to the training split T, |T| = N. For i in T let v_i in R^d be the frozen reference TARGET representation, u_i = v_i / ||v_i||_2 (u_i = 0 if ||v_i||_2 = 0), and p_i = exp_0^c(u_i) = tanh(sqrt(c)/2) * u_i / sqrt(c) (so for c = 1, p_i = tanh(0.5) * u_i). For x,y in B: d(x,y) = c^(-1/2) * arcosh( 1 + 2c*||x-y||_2^2 / ((1 - c*||x||_2^2)*(1 - c*||y||_2^2)) ). For each level-1 code value k present in T: C_k = {i in T : code_i[1] = k}, n_k = |C_k|, K = number of nonempty k. b_k = argmin_{b in B} sum_{i in C_k} d(b,p_i)^2, the geodesic Frechet (Karcher) barycentre. a_k = (1/n_k) * sum_{i in C_k} d(p_i,b_k) if n_k >= 2, else a_k = 0. s_k = min_{j != k, n_j >= 2} d(b_k,b_j) if such j exists, else s_k = 0. q_k = (s_k - a_k)/max(s_k,a_k) if n_k >= 2 and max(s_k,a_k) > 0, else q_k = 0. M = (1/N) * sum_k n_k * q_k; if K = 1, M = -1. M is in [-1,1]; higher is better.
INPUTS: (1) the exported Stage-2 SID table, integer array [n_items, L]; only column 1 (the level-1 code) is read. (2) the frozen Issue #126 reference, per-item TARGET representation array [n_items, d]; the source query side is not read. (3) the training-split item index list or boolean mask. Nothing else: no validation interaction, no test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 output, no fitted quantity.
GEOMETRY: Curvature -c with c = 1. Every item is placed by the Poincare exponential map at the origin, exp_0^c, so every item lies on the hyperbolic sphere of radius 1 (Euclidean radius tanh(1/2) = 0.462). All distances are Poincare geodesic distances d. Every cell centre b_k is a geodesic Frechet (Karcher) barycentre computed with Poincare log/exp: b_k^(0) = p_{i0} for the smallest-index i0 in C_k; for t = 0..49, b_k^(t+1) = exp_{b_k^(t)}( (1/n_k) * sum_{i in C_k} log_{b_k^(t)}(p_i) ), stopping early if ||(1/n_k) sum_i log_{b_k^(t)}(p_i)||_2 < 1e-8. Here log_x(y) = 2*artanh(||(-x) (+) y||_2) * ((-x) (+) y)/||(-x) (+) y||_2, exp_x(w) = x (+) (tanh(||w||_2/2) * w/||w||_2), and x (+) y = ((1 + 2<x,y> + ||y||_2^2) x + (1 - ||x||_2^2) y)/(1 + 2<x,y> + ||x||_2^2 ||y||_2^2). Curvature enters in three places: (i) the exp_0 placement is not the identity; (ii) d is the hyperbolic distance, not ||x-y||_2; (iii) b_k is a hyperbolic barycentre, which unlike a Euclidean centroid of points on a sphere is pulled toward the origin as a cell becomes angularly diffuse. A Euclidean silhouette on cosine centroids would be a different number and is not what is computed.
WHY IT SHOULD TRACK RECALL: Stage-3 Recall@10 is left-to-right SID generation: the first level-1 code is chosen from 256 under a 10-beam. A level-1 partition helps recall when each cell is (a) semantically tight, so the first token is learnable, and (b) separated from every other cell, so the first token is discriminative and does not burn beam slots on a near-duplicate region. a_k and s_k measure those two quantities, and q_k is their normalized margin. Q_H is an ordinal prefix-ranking score: it asks whether sharing the level-1 prefix ranks reference neighbours above non-neighbours, but it is blind to the size of the margin, so two tables with identical ranking can have very different cell sharpness; the silhouette separates them. It cannot be raised by putting everything into one bucket (K = 1 gives -1) or by scattering cells (separation collapses), so it is not a bucket-count or same-bucket statistic. Level 1 is the only level with about N/256 = 96 items per code; deeper prefixes are nearly item identifiers, which is why Q_H falls at levels 2-3 and why deeper levels are deliberately excluded.
COMPUTE: N = 24587, d = reference dimension (typically 64 to 768), K <= 256. Normalize and exp_0: O(N*d). Karcher: at most 50 iterations of one log per item per cell, O(50*N*d) worst case (typically under 10 iterations). Cohesion a_k: N distances to the own cell centre. Separation s_k: O(K^2) centre-to-centre distances. Total well under one minute in NumPy, single pass, no pair sampling, no Stage-2 and no Stage-3 run.
RISKS: A strongly anisotropic reference with a large shared mean puts all p_i in a small cap, shrinking variance across the 97 tables. Level-1-only design misses tables that differ only in level-2 or level-3 structure, though those levels are near-unique at N = 24587 and B = 256. Karcher iteration is ill-conditioned for points near the boundary; use the arcosh-safe distance and the 50-iteration cap. A table with very few, very pure cells can score well even though 10-beam resolution is coarse; the size-weighted cohesion term only partly offsets this. A pathological table with many singleton level-1 cells gets q_k = 0 for them, and one giant diffuse cell drives M toward -1. Reference representations that are dominated by popularity rather than semantic similarity would make the measured geometry irrelevant to retrieval.
FAILURE MODE: It must be worst (M closest to -1) on a table whose level-1 column is a semantic hash: codes assigned independently of the reference geometry, e.g. a random permutation of items into codes, item-id modulo 256, or a single code for all items. Then each cell is a diffuse mixture, a_k is near the maximum hyperbolic radius 1, the cell barycentres collapse toward the origin so s_k is small, every q_k is near -1, and M is near -1; the K = 1 table is -1 by definition. That is exactly the table that offers no usable coarse semantics to a 10-beam generator.
END METRIC"});
